text.p: Mexico's main leftist opposition party accused the government on Thursday of waging a dirty war against the party's supporters in the poor southern state of Oaxaca ahead of elections in July.

Officials of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) said a massacre of a party activist and her family in Oaxaca on Wednesday was the latest in a series of politically motivated killings in the region.
"(It is) a dirty war by the government so it can avoid losing the elections," Saul Vicente, head of the PRD in Oaxaca, told reporters.
Four people were killed in the town of Rio Grande, some 250 miles (400 km) south of the state capital on Wednesday.
The attorney general's office for the state of Oaxaca said in a statement late on Thursday that it would undertake an "in-depth" investigation of the killings.
It said Silvano Martinez Salinas, 39, Maria Carro Vargas, 75, Mario Martinez Vargas, 15, and Oliva Vargas Jimenez, 42, were killed in the incident.
The state government said that Oliva Vargas Jimenez had a shotgun fired into her mouth and was shot numerous times with an M-1 rifle.
Officials at the Mexico City headquarters for the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) were not available for comment on the accusations.

At least seven democratic revolution activists in Oaxaca have been gunned down in the past three months -- in the campaigns leading to national elections on July 6, when Mexicans will elect most of a new Congress, six state governors and a mayor for Mexico City.
In April, a well-known PRD candidate for the lower house of Congress was arrested and beaten by local authorities.
Party leaders claim the institutional party has aimed repression at impoverished areas that were likely to vote for the opposition in local races.

The PRD has also accused the government of harassment in the neighbouring state of Guerrero last week after the army arrested seven of its activists and charged them with belonging to a leftist rebel group, the Popular Revolutionary Army.

Among the PRD members murdered in Oaxaca were the mayor of Jamiltepec, a small town 100 miles (160 km) southwest of the state capital, and other PRD officials in several Oaxaca towns including Santiago Tetepec and Santa Maria Huazolotitlan.
